doctrine_note: Round 2 is a coordination pass, not a second forecast. The incoming handoff confirmed my round-1 extension rather than changing it, so the number HOLDS at -900 and I say so plainly - a confirmation is not an improvement and manufacturing 90 dollars of movement toward a visible actual would be fitting, not refinement. cross_cutting_mbo_finding.headline: ROUND 2 REBUILDS THIS FINDING AND RETRACTS THREE OF ITS FOUR ROUND-1 CLAIMS. The surviving mechanism is narrower, measured on four blocks, and falsifiable: THE BLIND RUNS A REAL MEAN-REVERSION RULE ON A FICTITIOUS STATE VARIABLE. The market mean-reverts against its REALIZED cum-from-anchor in every block measured (corr -0.36 / -0.58 / -0.63 / -0.50 for G17/G18/G19/G20). The blind mean-reverts against its CONSTRUCTED cum (corr of its own day-guess against its own running chain: -0.65 / -0.18 / -0.71 / -0.52). The rule is right; the input is a forecast integral, not a market state. Separately and NOT the same thing, the blind carries a persistent DOWN BIAS (mean per-day error -206 USD over 40 days, its constructed chain negative on 36 of 40 days) - and that bias, not the chain-staleness, is what produces the block lean.

what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.claim: 'a continuous chain integrates the blind's own directional error WITHOUT BOUND'
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.verdict: RETRACTED - falsified by my own data.
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.measurement: mean |divergence| by session index k across G17-G20: k=1 768, k=2 590, k=3 1022, k=4 2182, k=5 2408, k=6 2645, k=7 2730, k=8 2388, k=9 2612, k=10 2058. A pure random walk on the measured per-day error sd (811) would grow as 811*sqrt(k): 811, 1147, 1405, 1622, 1813, 1986, 2146, 2294, 2433, 2565. The observed divergence tracks the envelope to k=4 and then SATURATES near 2,400-2,700 while the envelope keeps rising, and at k=10 it is BELOW it. The divergence is bounded and sub-diffusive, not unbounded. The word 'unbounded' was rhetoric and it is wrong.

what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.claim: 'one integrator, opposite signs, ALLOCATED BY DAY-CLASS - 4,050 too low on eight mid-week days, 1,490 too high on the two Monday-class days'
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.verdict: RETRACTED - it is a G20-only artifact and G19 inverts it.
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.measurement: G19 signed error by class: Monday-class -3,400 (n=2, blind TOO LOW), non-Monday +1,030 (n=8). G20: Monday-class +1,490 (TOO HIGH), non-Monday -4,050. Exactly opposite allocations on consecutive blocks. The coordinator's independent G17-G20 day-class means (Mon -465, Tue +24, Wed -60, Thu -692, Fri +165) agree with G19 and against my G20 reading: across four blocks the blind's Monday bias is NEGATIVE, and its largest day-class bias is THURSDAY (-692, the EIA print), which my story does not address at all. A mechanism that predicted a stable sign allocation and delivered opposite signs on consecutive blocks is refuted on its own prediction.

what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.claim: 'polarity INVERTED at my seam' as the causal driver of the miss
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.verdict: RETRACTED AS A MECHANISM, KEPT AS A DESCRIPTION OF ONE DAY.
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.measurement: Direct test over all 40 block-days: days where sign(constructed cum) != sign(realized cum) have mean |err| 660 (n=27); days where the signs AGREE have mean |err| 677 (n=9). No difference. Polarity inversion does not predict a larger error. It was true on 0601 and it explains nothing general.

what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.claim: 'the measurement' - the divergence table offered as evidence
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.verdict: RETRACTED AS EVIDENCE. It is an IDENTITY.
what_I_retract_from_round_1_and_why.measurement: divergence_t = realized_cum_t - constructed_cum_t = -(sum of the blind's errors through t), verified exactly on all four blocks (residual 0 on 40/40 days). The divergence IS the running integral of the errors it was offered to explain. Quoting 'mean |divergence| = 2,310 = 2.1x n0_range_20_mean' as a finding restates 'the blind's errors accumulated'. It is a useful bookkeeping object and it is not evidence for any causal claim. I should have caught this in round 1.

what_survives_and_the_measurement_that_e.premise_1_the_market_side: The market mean-reverts against realized cum-from-anchor. corr(actual day-move_t, realized cum_{t-1}) = -0.361 (G17), -0.578 (G18), -0.631 (G19), -0.500 (G20); pooled -0.324 over 40 days. NEGATIVE IN ALL FOUR BLOCKS. Note it is a LEVEL effect, not a momentum effect: the lag-1 autocorrelation of the actual day-move is -0.045, i.e. nothing. Days do not alternate; days revert against the accumulated level.
what_survives_and_the_measurement_that_e.premise_2_the_blind_side: The blind applies that same reversion, to its own chain. corr(blind day-guess_t, constructed cum_{t-1}) = -0.653 (G17), -0.177 (G18), -0.705 (G19), -0.520 (G20). NEGATIVE IN ALL FOUR BLOCKS.
what_survives_and_the_measurement_that_e.the_consequence_which_is_what_round_1_sa: corr(blind error_t, divergence_{t-1}) = +0.503 / +0.397 / +0.659 / +0.465, positive in all four blocks. Under an independent-error null this correlation is ZERO (the divergence is the running negative sum of past errors, which is uncorrelated with the next error), so it is not an artifact of the identity above - it is the joint footprint of premises 1 and 2. Note its SIGN is the opposite of what my round-1 story predicted: I claimed a chain running low would drag the next guess LOW (negative feedback into the error); the measurement says a chain running low is followed by guesses that are TOO HIGH. That is the reversion rule firing on the wrong variable, not a runaway integrator.
what_survives_and_the_measurement_that_e.how_much_the_missing_variable_is_worth: Leave-one-block-out benchmark of a ONE-VARIABLE rule that uses NOTHING but the realized cum: day-move_hat = -beta * realized_cum_{t-1}, beta fitted on the other three blocks and scored on the held-out block. Held-out G17: mean|err| 353 vs the blind's 451. G18: 563 vs 521 (the one loss). G19: 779 vs 939. G20: 713 vs 788. Direction hits 4/5/4/6 against the blind's 5/5/4/6. One number the blind is masked from, with no weather, no storage, no positioning, no flow and no calendar, matches or beats the entire blind stack on day-level error in three blocks of four.
what_survives_and_the_measurement_that_e.the_part_this_does_NOT_explain_stated_be: It does NOT explain the block lean. The same one-variable rule's forward-curve drift on the held-out blocks is +1,135 / -1,077 / -3,842 / -3,345 against the blind's -970 / -2,330 / -2,370 / -2,560: on G19 and G20 the cum-reversion rule leans DOWN HARDER than the blind does. Cum-blindness is a DISPERSION problem, not a DRIFT problem. The drift is a separate defect - a flat down bias in the blind's day-guesses (mean -206/day; constructed block cum negative in all four blocks at -2,040 / -1,720 / -1,220 / -700 while the actual block cum ran -1,070 / +610 / +1,150 / +1,860). Round 1 claimed one mechanism produced both. Two mechanisms produce them, and fixing the one I named would make the drift worse.

the_falsifier_what_would_kill_this.F1_kills_the_market_premise: A block with corr(actual day-move_t, realized cum_{t-1}) >= 0. Four for four negative so far; one non-negative block is a serious hit, two kills the premise and with it the whole mechanism, because if the market does not revert against cum there is nothing for a wrong cum to get wrong.
the_falsifier_what_would_kill_this.F2_kills_the_blind_premise: A block with corr(blind day-guess_t, constructed cum_{t-1}) >= 0. That would mean the blind is not running a cum-reversion rule at all, and the mechanism has no blind-side half.
the_falsifier_what_would_kill_this.F3_kills_the_worth_claim: The leave-one-block-out one-variable benchmark ceasing to match or beat the blind's mean|err| on new blocks. It is already 3 of 4, not 4 of 4 - G18 is a recorded loss and I am not hiding it.
the_falsifier_what_would_kill_this.F4_the_guard_against_the_A_trap: The G19 post-mortem killed covering-self-limiting because it was non-falsifiable toward DOWN - unfired implied down AND spent implied down. This finding is exposed to the same disease because it can narrate an error of either sign. The guard is that it is now stated as TWO SIGNED CORRELATIONS with a predicted sign each (F1 negative, F2 negative) and a predicted sign for their product (F3, err vs divergence POSITIVE), and every one of those three can come out the other way on the next block. Concretely: if G21's blind runs error and divergence with a NEGATIVE correlation, my round-1 runaway-integrator story would be the live hypothesis and this round-2 one would be dead. I could not say that in round 1, and that is the difference between the two versions.
the_falsifier_what_would_kill_this.F5_what_would_have_killed_it_in_round_1_: The day-class allocation and the unbounded-growth claims both made predictions, both were checkable against G19, and both failed. I ran the checks and they are recorded above rather than quietly dropped.

does_it_survive_on_G19.answer: The mechanism survives on G19 and is STRONGEST there. The round-1 STORY does not survive on G19 and is retracted.
does_it_survive_on_G19.survives: G19 has the largest market-side reversion (-0.631), the largest blind-side reversion (-0.705) and the largest error-vs-divergence coupling (+0.659) of the four blocks. G19 is the cleanest instance of the mechanism, not a counterexample to it.
does_it_survive_on_G19.does_not_survive: The day-class allocation inverts (G19 Monday-class -3,400 too LOW vs G20 +1,490 too HIGH). The unbounded-integration claim is contradicted by G19's own divergence path, which peaks at 5,120 on k=7 and then FALLS to 2,370 by k=10 - the market came back to the chain rather than the chain running away.
does_it_survive_on_G19.the_shared_fingerprint_that_is_real: In both blocks the blind's constructed chain was NEGATIVE across essentially the whole block (9/10 days in G19, 7/10 in G20) while the realized chain was POSITIVE across essentially the whole block. Both blinds spent the block believing the market was below its anchor while it was above. That is the same fingerprint - but it is a BIAS fingerprint, not a staleness fingerprint, and it points at the down bias in premise-free day-guesses rather than at chain continuity.

the_blind_side_observable_the_crux.the_question: The blind cannot compute the divergence - it has no realized cum. So chain_staleness_gate is useless unless there is an OPEN-TIME, NEVER-MASKED proxy for the extension state. I tested every candidate in the never-masked set. Each was tested against realized cum-from-anchor on G18/G19/G20 (G17 has no committed state file).

candidates_tested_and_rejected_per_event.verdict: REJECTED. The sign FLIPS between a normal block and a covering block, and it flips toward NEGATIVE exactly in the covering regimes where an extension gate matters most. In G20 the tape ran four consecutive net-sell sessions (cum -9,198) under a +2,710 price rally. A flow integral is not a price integral; in a covering rally it is its mirror image.

REJECTED twice over. Sign-unstable, and it takes only TWO distinct values inside a ten-session block (report dates 05-19 and 05-26 in G20), so the correlation is a two-point comparison dressed as a statistic. It is also structurally late: G20's 05-26 report covers the week BEFORE the 05-27/05-28 rally, so at the 0601 seam it reported the short getting MORE crowded (WoW -38,123) while the price had already run +2,710.

candidates_tested_and_rejected_per_event.measurement: corr with |realized cum_{t-1}|: +0.556 / +0.799 / +0.832 - which looks promising until it is compared to the session counter alone: corr(k, |realized cum|) = +0.562 / +0.785 / +0.811. Identical. And volume IN EXCESS of the block's own opening run-rate correlates -0.332 / -0.644 / +0.832 - sign-unstable.
candidates_tested_and_rejected_per_event.verdict: REJECTED. Cumulative volume is a CLOCK in disguise; it carries no information about extension beyond 'more sessions have happened'.
AVAILABLE, FREE, AND THE ONLY SURVIVOR - but it gives only the MAGNITUDE envelope of the extension, never its SIGN. It cannot tell an extension-gated play which side to fade.

the_blind_side_observable_the_crux.the_plain_answer: NO BLIND-SIDE OBSERVABLE OF THE SIGN OR LEVEL OF REALIZED CUM EXISTS IN THE CURRENT NEVER-MASKED SET. I name that rather than manufacture a proxy. The consequence is that chain_staleness_gate CANNOT be divergence-triggered on the blind side, and my round-1 threshold ('stand down when the staleness term exceeds ~1x n0_range_20_mean') is not runnable by the blind as written. It is a refine-only gate in that form, which makes it useless where the problem is.

what_IS_runnable_the_honest_reduction.name: chain_staleness_gate, DETERMINISTIC form (proposal only, no brain edit in this run)
what_IS_runnable_the_honest_reduction.rule: The blind's constructed chain has a MEASURED dispersion around the realized chain that depends only on k, the session index from the block anchor - and k is known in advance for a one-shot block blind, so this is not a runtime signal, it is a schedule. Measured mean |divergence|: k<=3 gives 768 / 590 / 1,022 (all below one n0_range_20_mean, ~1,094); k>=4 gives 2,182 / 2,408 / 2,645 / 2,730 / 2,388 / 2,612 / 2,058 (all roughly 2x it). So: a play keyed on cum_from_anchor or chain extension may assert a RUNG for k<=3; from k>=4 it must widen to the full band or stand down and hand the decision to a channel with no cum content.
what_IS_runnable_the_honest_reduction.what_it_would_have_done_on_0601: 0601 is k=6. The blind's day sign came from boundary.seam_gap_up_prior_on_worsening_cot's RUNG-2 intraday arm, which is cum-keyed ('at high extension it round-trips to ~0 and the day IS the gap'). Under the gate that arm stands down and the day routes to the non-cum-keyed gates - monday.catchup_window_tilt_gate (D-1 trade tilt) and daytype.monday_weekend_gap R3. The GAP arm of the seam play is not cum-keyed and survives, which is correct: the gap was right at +690.
what_IS_runnable_the_honest_reduction.the_honest_cost: This gate makes the blind SILENT on extension for two thirds of every block. That is an unwelcome answer and I am not going to dress it up. The measured alternative is worse: on the seven k>=4 days per block the constructed chain is on average 2,400 USD away from the realized one, which is 2.2x n0_range_20_mean, and asserting a rung off it is asserting a rung off noise.
what_IS_runnable_the_honest_reduction.forward_test: On G21+, record for each day whether any cum-keyed play fired and at what k. The prediction is that the blind's |err| on k>=4 days where a cum-keyed play fired exceeds its |err| on k>=4 days where none did. If that difference is zero or negative the gate is worthless and should be dropped.

the_finding_I_did_not_have_in_round_1_an.headline: ON 0601 THE BLIND WAS NOT SERVED THE FRIDAY'S FLOW AT ALL. My round-1 selection_reason said the blind 'owed the day' to monday.catchup_window_tilt_gate and had the D-1 tilt 'in hand'. THAT IS WRONG AND I RETRACT IT. The Friday 05-29 session is served NOWHERE in G20's decision state.
the_finding_I_did_not_have_in_round_1_an.the_audit: tape_conditions.session by day across G20: 0525<-0524, 0526<-0525, 0527<-0526, 0528<-0527, 0529<-0528, 0601<-20260531, 0602<-0601, 0603<-0602, 0604<-0603, 0605<-0604. Session 20260529 appears in NO day's tape_conditions. On the Monday the blind was served the SUNDAY REOPEN STUB: 2,620 lots, 1,224 trades, session_signed_flow +278. The dropped Friday session was ~117,069 lots with total_sflow -2,126. The blind's single strongest non-price directional channel, on the highest-stakes day of the week, was replaced by a sample 2.2% of its size whose sign was OPPOSITE (+278 vs -2,126). The blind called +350.
the_finding_I_did_not_have_in_round_1_an.it_is_systemic_not_a_one_day_accident: Same audit across every staged group: G21 0615 served a 123-lot stub in place of 0612; G22 0629 served a 375-lot stub in place of 0626; G23 0706 served a 251-lot stub and 0713 a 534-lot stub. Every Monday from G20 forward. G17/G18/G19 are clean (their Sunday reopens did not register as separate sessions), which is why this never showed up before and why it looks like a regression rather than an old bug.
the_finding_I_did_not_have_in_round_1_an.why_state_health_could_not_catch_it: This is S107's seventh silent hole and it is a NEW CLASS. The other six were EMPTY blocks. This block is fully populated - every field present, plausible values, never_masked TRUE - it is simply the WRONG SESSION. A completeness assertion cannot see it. The detector for this class is a CONSISTENCY assertion: the session tape_conditions serves must be the prior TRADING session in the block, and if it is not, both must be carried.
the_finding_I_did_not_have_in_round_1_an.attribution_kept_straight_as_the_directi: The harness fix already landed THIS SESSION (commit 2a36fa2, 'Fix the Monday stub: the blind now carries the Friday too'; forecast_harness._tape_conditions_block now sets prior_session_is_reopen_stub and attaches prior_full_session). I verified it is present in the restaged G21 and G22 states (G21 0615 carries prior_full_session 20260612 at 74,362 lots; G22 0629 carries 20260626 at 121,487) and ABSENT from G23's two Mondays, which have not been restaged. So this is not my discovery of an open defect - it is my measurement of WHAT THE DEFECT COST on the day I own, plus one open item: G23 still needs a restage before it can be run.
the_finding_I_did_not_have_in_round_1_an.what_it_changes_for_the_merge: It changes the verdict on my own day and it partly vindicates A, whom I overrode in round 1. I ruled the blind's miss 'a failure to consult two incumbent gates'. It was not. monday.catchup_window_tilt_gate requires the D-1 trade tilt; the tilt the blind was served was +278 UP, and consulting the gate on the served state would have produced the SAME +350 it printed. The blind could not have run that gate correctly from the state it was given. A's position that the brain lacked something is closer to right than mine was - though A located the lack in a missing RUNG and it was actually a missing INPUT. My round-1 magnitude, direction and derivation are unaffected (they were never sourced from the blind's served state), but the ATTRIBUTION is: this day was lost to a data defect first and a reasoning gap second, and a merge must not bank the correction as forward evidence for any play.
